units.source_excerpt: For Problem 1, we build a Target-two-Players-Lost (T2PL) dynamic system based on SIR
units.function: announce the first model by problem number
units.reusable_pattern: Open each summary paragraph with For Problem N, we build/develop/perform, then name the model.
information_order: problem number then verb then model name
prohibited_generalizations: Do not flatten the five problem paragraphs into one abstract sentence.

units.source_excerpt: with general vs loyal players and different attrition rates, plus word-attribute effects on Hard Mode percentage
units.function: state what the model adds beyond its base
units.reusable_pattern: After the model name, add the contrast the model introduces and the extra effect it explains.
information_order: contrast then extra effect
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the second thing the model is said to explain.

units.source_excerpt: For Problem 2, we develop a P&S Model that eliminates unsatisfactory words then samples by word frequency
units.function: announce the second model and its two steps
units.reusable_pattern: Name the model, then give its two mechanical steps in then order.
information_order: model name then step then step
prohibited_generalizations: Do not describe the simulation without the rescaling step.

units.source_excerpt: predicting EERIE on March 1, 2023 as (0, 0, 9%, 29%, 45%, 14%, 3%)
units.function: close a method paragraph with one concrete prediction
units.reusable_pattern: End the method sentence with the single number the reader will remember.
information_order: method then one printed tuple
prohibited_generalizations: Do not round or reformat the printed distribution.

units.source_excerpt: For Problem 3, we perform three-cluster K-means labeled easy/medium/hard plus a Random Forest
units.function: announce the third method as a pair
units.reusable_pattern: Pair the unsupervised step with the supervised step in one sentence.
information_order: cluster then classifier
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report the cluster labels without saying what produced them.

units.source_excerpt: For Problem 4, linear regression showing harder puzzles produce fewer reports
units.function: announce the last method by its conclusion
units.reusable_pattern: State the regression and the direction of its finding in the same breath.
information_order: method then direction of effect
prohibited_generalizations: Do not quote the regression without its sign.

units.source_excerpt: Keywords: Wordle; Dynamic system; Simulation; K-means; Random Forest
units.function: list the method names as keywords
units.reusable_pattern: Close the summary with a semicolon keyword line naming each method once.
information_order: keyword line
prohibited_generalizations: Do not invent keywords the paper does not print.

units.source_excerpt: Wordle is a popular puzzle currently offered daily by the New York Times
units.function: open with the object and its owner
units.reusable_pattern: Open the background by naming the thing and the institution that runs it.
information_order: object then owner
prohibited_generalizations: Do not open with a general claim about games.

units.source_excerpt: As we know it, the game gives six chances to guess a five-letter word
units.function: explain the rules as shared knowledge
units.reusable_pattern: Use as we know it to mark a rule the reader is assumed to share.
information_order: shared-knowledge marker then rule
prohibited_generalizations: Do not explain rules the paper treats as obvious.

units.source_excerpt: Based on the current situation and the requirements of the problem, we need to
units.function: pivot from background to the task list
units.reusable_pattern: Bridge background to tasks with based on the current situation and the requirements.
information_order: situation then requirements then we need to
reusable_elements: Based on the current situation and the requirements of the problem
prohibited_generalizations: Do not jump from background to equations.

units.source_excerpt: Firstly, we extract 12 attribute indicators. Secondly, we build the dynamic system. Thirdly, we simulate.
units.function: preview the paper as a numbered sequence
units.reusable_pattern: Preview the whole paper with Firstly, Secondly, Thirdly, Fourthly, Finally.
information_order: ordinal adverb then verb then object
prohibited_generalizations: Do not preview with a bulleted list when the paper uses ordinal adverbs.

units.source_excerpt: Predict the number of reported results on March 1, 2023 and give a prediction interval
units.function: restate the first contest task
units.reusable_pattern: Restate each contest task as a bare imperative with its date.
information_order: verb then quantity then date
prohibited_generalizations: Do not merge two contest tasks into one.

units.source_excerpt: Develop a model to predict the distribution of the reported results for a given word
units.function: restate the second contest task
units.reusable_pattern: Keep develop a model as the verb when the task asks for a distribution.
information_order: develop a model then target
prohibited_generalizations: Do not name the model inside the restatement.

units.source_excerpt: Classify the difficulty of the solution word and identify which attributes matter
units.function: restate the third contest task
units.reusable_pattern: Pair the classification task with the attribute task in one restatement.
information_order: classify then identify
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a difficulty scale the contest did not ask for.

units.source_excerpt: There is no shift in the general trend of daily users
units.function: state an assumption as a flat denial
units.reusable_pattern: Write an assumption as there is no X, not as we assume that.
information_order: there is no then quantity
prohibited_generalizations: Do not soften an assumption the paper states flatly.

units.source_excerpt: Most players use rational strategies and make no unessential moves
units.function: restrict player behaviour by a named exclusion
units.reusable_pattern: State the behaviour, then name the thing excluded in quotes.
information_order: most X do Y, no Z
prohibited_generalizations: Do not generalise rational to all players.

units.source_excerpt: There is no significant skill change because experienced players quit while rookies join
units.function: justify an assumption with a cancelling pair
units.reusable_pattern: Justify a no-change assumption by two movements that cancel.
information_order: no change because A while B
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the cancelling mechanism.

units.source_excerpt: For convenience, in Task 2 players and sharers are not distinguished
units.function: flag a simplifying assumption with for convenience
units.reusable_pattern: Mark a convenience assumption with for convenience, then state what is collapsed.
information_order: for convenience then collapse
prohibited_generalizations: Do not hide a convenience assumption inside the model.

units.source_excerpt: N is the number of reported results, H the hard-mode reports, PH the percentage
units.function: define the three report symbols together
units.reusable_pattern: Define the count, the subset count and the ratio in one line.
information_order: symbol then symbol then ratio
prohibited_generalizations: Do not define the ratio without both counts.

units.source_excerpt: Word attribute indicators is not included, because they are explaned in detail below
units.function: defer a symbol block and keep the printed slip
units.reusable_pattern: Point forward to a later section instead of repeating a table, and keep the printed spelling.
information_order: not included because explained below
prohibited_generalizations: Do not correct explaned or the agreement error.

units.source_excerpt: The data set Problem_C_Data_Wordle.xlsx covers 359 days and has no missing values
units.function: open preprocessing with file name, span and a clean bill
units.reusable_pattern: Name the file, the day count and the missing-value status in one sentence.
information_order: file then span then missing status
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim missing values were imputed.

units.source_excerpt: Table 2 corrects rprobe to probe, naive to naive, clen to clean, marxh to marsh, tash to trash
units.function: list spelling repairs as a table
units.reusable_pattern: Report each repair as wrong form to right form, tied to its contest number.
information_order: wrong to right, contest number
prohibited_generalizations: Do not apply the repairs silently.

units.source_excerpt: Question 281 nymph on 2022/3/27 has percentages summing to 126, so the row is dropped
units.function: drop one row and give the reason in the same sentence
units.reusable_pattern: Name the word, the date, the impossible sum, then the action.
information_order: case then impossible number then dropped
prohibited_generalizations: Do not repair the row to sum to 100.

units.source_excerpt: Question 529 study on 2022/11/30 reported 2569, corrected to 25690, with hard mode 2405
units.function: state one magnitude correction with both numbers
units.reusable_pattern: Give the printed value and the corrected value side by side.
information_order: printed then corrected
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the printed 2569.

units.source_excerpt: Figure 2, a calendar map, shows no weekly pattern, so the fluctuation is attributed to trend plus word difficulty
units.function: read a figure as a negative finding and draw the consequence
units.reusable_pattern: State what the figure does not show, then name the two causes that remain.
information_order: no pattern so cause plus cause
prohibited_generalizations: Do not invent a weekly effect.

units.source_excerpt: We select 12 indicators in four families: familiarity, composition, association and confusion
units.function: announce an indicator set by its families
units.reusable_pattern: Give the count, then the family names, before any formula.
information_order: count then four family names
prohibited_generalizations: Do not list formulas before the families.

units.source_excerpt: For example, Nc of apple is 2 and Nc of mummy is 3, because players do not try the same letter twice
units.function: define an indicator by two toy words and a player habit
units.reusable_pattern: Define a count with two quoted words, then the habit that makes it matter.
information_order: example pair then because habit
prohibited_generalizations: Do not define Nc without the examples.

units.source_excerpt: The greater Nc, the less likely the word is to be guessed
units.function: state the expected direction before any fit
units.reusable_pattern: Use the greater X, the less likely Y as a prior, not a result.
information_order: the greater X the less Y
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present this direction as a fitted coefficient.

units.source_excerpt: The greater the letter frequency sum, the greater the probability of yellow tiles appearing
units.function: tie an indicator to a visible game event
units.reusable_pattern: Connect the indicator to the tile colour the player actually sees.
information_order: the greater X the greater the probability of Y
prohibited_generalizations: Do not leave the indicator without its tile colour.

units.source_excerpt: Greater NFI2 increases the probability of information gain by close guesses, so it is assumed to be easier
units.function: mark a direction as an assumption
units.reusable_pattern: When a direction is guessed, say it is assumed to be, not it is.
information_order: mechanism so assumed direction
reusable_elements: so it is assumed to be
prohibited_generalizations: Do not upgrade an assumed direction to a finding.

units.source_excerpt: When ND1 and ND2 are high, a player may need more tries to verify which similar word is right, and is more likely to fail
units.function: explain a high indicator as extra verification work
units.reusable_pattern: Give the mechanism (more candidates to check) before the failure consequence.
information_order: high count then more tries then more failure
reusable_elements: may need to spend more times
prohibited_generalizations: Do not correct spend more times.

units.source_excerpt: It is obvious that Wordle has become viral last year
units.function: open a model section with an obvious fact
units.reusable_pattern: Start the analysis with it is obvious that, then the fact the model must capture.
information_order: it is obvious that then fact
prohibited_generalizations: Do not open a model section with the equations.

units.source_excerpt: Shared tweets rise at an exponential rate, then drop gradually after March, so the tendency could be captured by an SIR model
units.function: justify a borrowed model by the shape of the curve
units.reusable_pattern: Describe the rise and the fall, then name the borrowed model and its original purpose.
information_order: shape then borrowed model then original use
prohibited_generalizations: Do not cite SIR without saying what it was built for.

units.source_excerpt: Like SIR, we can assume three groups: targeted population, current players, and lost players
units.function: import a model's compartments with like X we can assume
units.reusable_pattern: Borrow compartments with like X, we can assume, then list them.
information_order: like X we can assume then list
reusable_elements: Like SIR model, we can assume
prohibited_generalizations: Do not rename the compartments without the list.

units.source_excerpt: However, this model failed to satisfy both the sharp decrease after the peak and the mild decrease later
units.function: reject the first model by naming the two shapes it misses
units.reusable_pattern: Reject a model with however, this model failed to, and name both missed shapes.
information_order: however failed to then shape and shape
reusable_elements: However, this model failed to satisfy both
prohibited_generalizations: Do not reject a model without saying which feature it misses.

units.source_excerpt: Therefore we improved the model by dividing players into loyal players and general players, which is named T2PL
units.function: introduce the improvement and name it in the same sentence
units.reusable_pattern: State the split, then name the model with which is named.
information_order: therefore we improved by dividing, named
reusable_elements: Therefore, we improved the model by
prohibited_generalizations: Do not introduce the name before the improvement.

units.source_excerpt: In case there were players who want to try Wordle again, an additional variable theta describes the lost-return rate
units.function: add a term by imagining the case it covers
units.reusable_pattern: Motivate an extra parameter with in case, then name it.
information_order: in case then variable
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a parameter without the case it answers.

units.source_excerpt: The objective is the mean square error between 1 and the ratio of estimated to actual, re-scaled because the range is too large
units.function: justify a non-standard loss by the scale of the data
units.reusable_pattern: Give the loss, then the because clause that explains the re-scaling.
information_order: loss then because range too large
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report the loss without the re-scaling reason.

units.source_excerpt: Without explicitly solving the function, our team use an auto-gradient package to optimize the parameters
units.function: name the tool and the thing it avoids
units.reusable_pattern: Say what is not done, then name the package that replaces it.
information_order: without X our team use Y
prohibited_generalizations: Do not correct the agreement in our team use.

units.source_excerpt: As long as the initial value is roughly the correct scale, it will find the local minimum
units.function: state the condition under which the optimizer is trusted
units.reusable_pattern: Qualify a numerical result with as long as, then the condition.
information_order: as long as condition then result
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim a global minimum.

units.source_excerpt: After 5000 epochs of training with learning rate 0.01, we find the optimal value of each variable
units.function: report the training budget before the values
units.reusable_pattern: Give epoch count and learning rate, then say we find the optimal value.
information_order: budget then we find
prohibited_generalizations: Do not omit the learning rate.

units.source_excerpt: The model is proved to excellently capture the tendency of reported Wordle results in 2022
units.function: praise the fit in the paper's own words
units.reusable_pattern: Evaluate a fit with is proved to excellently capture, not with a metric alone.
information_order: is proved to excellently capture
prohibited_generalizations: Do not replace the praise with a neutral verb.

units.source_excerpt: On 2023.3.1 it is predicted to have 19367 users sending Wordle results
units.function: give the point prediction with its date
units.reusable_pattern: State the date in the paper's dotted form, then the integer.
information_order: date then predicted count
prohibited_generalizations: Do not round 19367.

units.source_excerpt: Because the model cannot provide a range by itself, we estimate by considering the MAPE
units.function: justify an interval method by what the model lacks
units.reusable_pattern: Say what the model cannot do, then the substitute measure.
information_order: cannot provide so we estimate by
reusable_elements: Because the model cannot provide a range of possible prediction by itself
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the interval as a model output.

units.source_excerpt: Given MAPE = 0.083, we can assume the result will fall within plus or minus MAPE, giving [17760, 20976]
units.function: turn an error into an interval with we can assume
units.reusable_pattern: State the error, the assumption, then the printed interval.
information_order: given error we can assume then interval
reusable_elements: we can assume the result will fall within
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call this a confidence interval without the paper's own hedge.

units.source_excerpt: The model predicts that there will be only 19% general players on 31 December 2022 and 21% on 1 March 2023
units.function: read a structural conclusion off the fitted curves
units.reusable_pattern: Give both dates and both shares, then the word only.
information_order: only X percent on date and Y percent on date
prohibited_generalizations: Do not merge the two dates.

units.source_excerpt: This overall trend can perhaps be explained by the change in player structure
units.function: offer an explanation with can perhaps
units.reusable_pattern: Attach can perhaps be explained by to a trend before asserting the cause.
information_order: trend can perhaps be explained by
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the hedge.

units.source_excerpt: To avoid the influence of the overall trend, the previous day's percentage is selected as the control variable
units.function: justify a control variable by the thing it removes
units.reusable_pattern: Name the nuisance, then the control chosen in order to avoid it.
information_order: in order to avoid X, Y is selected as the control
reusable_elements: In order to avoid the influence of
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a control without its purpose.

units.source_excerpt: The results show that F and LFsum have a significant negative effect, while Nc, LF4 and NFI2 have a significant positive effect
units.function: report regression signs grouped by direction
units.reusable_pattern: Group coefficients into negative then positive, each with while.
information_order: negative effect while positive effect
prohibited_generalizations: Do not list coefficients without their sign.

units.source_excerpt: And it can be found through the later analysis that these indicators determine the difficulty of words
units.function: point forward to a later section for the explanation
units.reusable_pattern: Defer the interpretation with it can be found through the later analysis.
information_order: and it can be found through the later analysis
prohibited_generalizations: Do not give the explanation before the paper does.

units.source_excerpt: Each step of the player's strategy depends on the previous word, so there are so many possibilities that it is almost impossible to calculate the probability
units.function: justify a simulation by an impossibility
units.reusable_pattern: Say why the exact probability cannot be computed, then introduce the simulation.
information_order: so many possibilities that almost impossible
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the simulation as a closed form.

units.source_excerpt: The main idea of the simulation algorithm is: players randomly select a word, then keep only the words consistent with the tiles
units.function: state an algorithm's idea before its pseudocode
units.reusable_pattern: Open with the main idea is, then the loop in one sentence.
information_order: the main idea is then loop
reusable_elements: The main idea of the simulation algorithm is
prohibited_generalizations: Do not start from the pseudocode.

units.source_excerpt: Note: here we assume that players know all the words in the dictionary D
units.function: park an assumption inside the algorithm as a note
units.reusable_pattern: Mark an algorithm assumption with Note: here we assume.
information_order: note here we assume
prohibited_generalizations: Do not bury the full-dictionary assumption.

units.source_excerpt: The error is 5.36%, which was not satisfactory
units.function: report a number and judge it in the same clause
units.reusable_pattern: Give the error, then a blunt which was not satisfactory.
information_order: number which was not satisfactory
prohibited_generalizations: Do not soften the paper's own verdict.

units.source_excerpt: We believe this is due to the fact that players who guessed quickly were more likely to share
units.function: explain a bias as a belief about behaviour
units.reusable_pattern: Use we believe this is due to the fact that for a behavioural explanation.
information_order: we believe this is due to the fact that
reusable_elements: We believe this is due to the fact that
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the sharing bias as measured.

units.source_excerpt: According to the above considerations, we propose the P&S (Played and Shared) model
units.function: name a correction model from the considerations above
units.reusable_pattern: Bridge with according to the above considerations, we propose, then expand the initials.
information_order: according to above we propose then expansion
reusable_elements: According to above considerations, we propose
prohibited_generalizations: Do not expand P&S differently from the paper.

units.source_excerpt: The error is reduced from 5.36% to 1.50%, which is a more desirable result
units.function: report an improvement as from X to Y
units.reusable_pattern: Give both errors and close with which is a more desirable result.
information_order: reduced from X to Y, more desirable
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report only the improved error.

units.source_excerpt: We speculated that the probability of each point will probably fall within plus or minus 1.50%
units.function: build an interval by speculation
units.reusable_pattern: Use we speculated that ... will probably fall within for a homemade interval.
information_order: we speculated then plus or minus
prohibited_generalizations: Do not call this a confidence interval.

units.source_excerpt: Due to the stochastic nature of the simulation, the prediction will not always be the same, which leads to some uncertainty
units.function: name the source of uncertainty plainly
units.reusable_pattern: Trace the uncertainty to one named property of the method.
information_order: due to X the result will not always be the same
prohibited_generalizations: Do not quantify an uncertainty the paper leaves qualitative.

units.source_excerpt: Puzzle designers seeking insight from this model would find it difficult to use this information
units.function: motivate a new model by the user's difficulty
units.reusable_pattern: Open a section with the person who would struggle, then what they need instead.
information_order: user would find it difficult so we build
reusable_elements: would find it difficult to use this information
prohibited_generalizations: Do not open with the algorithm.

units.source_excerpt: It is expected that a comprehensive label describing the difficulty will be created
units.function: state the deliverable as an expectation
units.reusable_pattern: Use it is expected that for the thing the section must produce.
information_order: it is expected that then deliverable
prohibited_generalizations: Do not promise more labels than the paper builds.

units.source_excerpt: For clustering algorithms, we compare two commonly used methods: k-means and the Gaussian mixture model
units.function: announce a comparison before choosing
units.reusable_pattern: Name both candidates with we compare two commonly used methods.
information_order: we compare A and B
reusable_elements: we compare two commonly used methods
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present k-means as the only option considered.

units.source_excerpt: The greater the silhouette value is, the more distinguishable the cluster would be
units.function: explain a metric by its direction
units.reusable_pattern: Gloss a metric with the greater X, the more Y.
information_order: the greater X the more Y
prohibited_generalizations: Do not correct the agreement error.

units.source_excerpt: Finally, we decide to create 3 clusters using k-means, although 2 classes score higher, because detailed classification is better
units.function: override a metric with a purpose
units.reusable_pattern: Concede the metric, then choose against it with although ... because.
information_order: although higher we choose lower because purpose
prohibited_generalizations: Do not hide that the chosen model scored worse.

units.source_excerpt: Figure 9 visualizes all three clusters, labeled easy, medium and hard according to the expected attempts of each centroid
units.function: name clusters from a property of their centroids
units.reusable_pattern: Say the figure, then the rule that assigns the names.
information_order: labeled according to
reusable_elements: labeled easy, medium and hard according to
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat the names as given by the algorithm.

units.source_excerpt: Random Forest has been shown to provide stable classification results on a wide range of data
units.function: justify an algorithm by a general reputation
units.reusable_pattern: Cite the algorithm's reputation with has been shown to, then the specific motive.
information_order: has been shown to then motivation
reusable_elements: has been shown to provide stable
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim a proof the paper does not give.

units.source_excerpt: The motivation of the algorithm is to reduce variance by bagging on the training set and the feature space
units.function: state an algorithm's motive in one line
units.reusable_pattern: Use the motivation of the algorithm is to for the design reason.
information_order: the motivation is to
reusable_elements: The motivation of the algorithm is to
prohibited_generalizations: Do not skip the motive.

units.source_excerpt: All records are split into 80% training and 20% testing
units.function: state the split before the metric
units.reusable_pattern: Give the split as two percentages before any score.
information_order: split into X and Y
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report accuracy without the split.

units.source_excerpt: It seems that the classification score is generally even among categories and the accuracy of 0.68 is high
units.function: judge a metric with it seems and the paper's own word high
units.reusable_pattern: Hedge with it seems that, then keep the paper's judgement that 0.68 is high.
information_order: it seems that then judgement
prohibited_generalizations: Do not contradict the paper's judgement in the learning record.

units.source_excerpt: The pattern is very obvious: a familiar word or an easily associated word is easier to guess
units.function: announce a pattern as obvious then state it
units.reusable_pattern: Open the reading with the pattern is very obvious.
information_order: the pattern is very obvious then statement
prohibited_generalizations: Do not bury the direction inside the figure.

units.source_excerpt: It is relatively less instinctive to try words with repeated letters, and players prefer to crack the vowel first
units.function: explain a sign by a player habit
units.reusable_pattern: Give the habit, then the correlation it produces.
information_order: less instinctive so correlated
reusable_elements: prefer to solve Wordle by cracking the vowel first
prohibited_generalizations: Do not report the sign without the habit.

units.source_excerpt: Based on our model, EERIE is classified as a hard answer, and the precision of this category is 0.58
units.function: apply the classifier to the contest word and attach its precision
units.reusable_pattern: State the label, then the precision of that class.
information_order: classified as then precision
prohibited_generalizations: Do not give the label without the class precision.

units.source_excerpt: Sensitivity analysis determines how the variations of an independent variable affect a dependent result
units.function: define the analysis before doing it
units.reusable_pattern: Open the section with a textbook definition of the analysis.
information_order: definition then purpose
prohibited_generalizations: Do not start from the perturbation.

units.source_excerpt: In the actual data the percentages may not sum to 100% due to rounding
units.function: motivate the perturbation by a real data defect
units.reusable_pattern: Name the defect first, then the test it inspires.
information_order: may not sum to 100 due to rounding
prohibited_generalizations: Do not invent a perturbation source.

units.source_excerpt: We assume the disturbance fluctuates randomly within 5% of the original data
units.function: state the perturbation range as an assumption
units.reusable_pattern: Give the range with we assume, tied to the uniform draw.
information_order: we assume then range
reusable_elements: fluctuates randomly in the range of 5%
prohibited_generalizations: Do not widen the 5% band.

units.source_excerpt: 3.34% of the clustering results changed, which indicates the results were not seriously affected and the model is relatively stable
units.function: turn a small change into a stability claim
units.reusable_pattern: Give the percentage, then which indicates ... not seriously affected.
information_order: percent changed which indicates stable
prohibited_generalizations: Do not upgrade relatively stable to robust.

units.source_excerpt: Since people are always more willing to share their better scores, we speculate that the fluctuation is related to difficulty
units.function: motivate a regression by a standing habit
units.reusable_pattern: Open with since plus a habit, then we speculate that.
information_order: since habit we speculate
reusable_elements: Since people are always more willing
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the speculation as a finding.

units.source_excerpt: The number of reported results is 6589.5 higher for an easy word, 1087.5 higher for a medium word, and 2649.3 lower for a hard word
units.function: report three dummy coefficients with their directions
units.reusable_pattern: Keep all three numbers and the words higher, higher, less.
information_order: three coefficients with direction
prohibited_generalizations: Do not round the printed coefficients.

units.source_excerpt: Because EERIE is hard, we subtracted 2649 from both endpoints, giving the corrected interval [15111, 18327]
units.function: revise an earlier interval with a new coefficient
units.reusable_pattern: Name the reason, the subtraction, then the new interval.
information_order: because hard we subtracted then new interval
reusable_elements: Because the word EERIE is hard
prohibited_generalizations: Do not replace the earlier interval; record both.

units.source_excerpt: Surprisingly, the Hard Mode percentage increases when the word is difficult and decreases when it is easy
units.function: flag a counterintuitive result with surprisingly
units.reusable_pattern: Open the finding with surprisingly, then both directions.
information_order: surprisingly then direction and direction
prohibited_generalizations: Do not smooth out the surprise.

units.source_excerpt: To investigate the reason for this phenomenon, we ran another two regressions
units.function: answer a surprise with more regressions
units.reusable_pattern: Follow a surprise with to investigate the reason, we ran another.
information_order: to investigate we ran another
reusable_elements: To investigate the reason for this phenomenon
prohibited_generalizations: Do not leave the surprise unexplained.

units.source_excerpt: Therefore we can analyze the reason: Hard Mode players keep sharing, Normal Mode players do not
units.function: close an investigation with the reason in plain terms
units.reusable_pattern: Use therefore we can analyze the reason, then the contrast.
information_order: therefore the reason then contrast
reusable_elements: Therefore, we can analyze the reason for this strange phenomenon
prohibited_generalizations: Do not attribute the effect to Hard Mode volume.

units.source_excerpt: The selection of evaluation indicators is scientific and easy to understand
units.function: open a strength with a self-judgement
units.reusable_pattern: Judge the work with is scientific and easy to understand.
information_order: selection is scientific and easy to understand
prohibited_generalizations: Do not replace the self-praise with a neutral summary.

units.source_excerpt: We have taken into account the game characteristics of Wordle and constructed four categories of indicators
units.function: support a strength by what was taken into account
units.reusable_pattern: Back the adjective with we have taken into account.
information_order: taken into account then constructed
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add categories beyond the four.

units.source_excerpt: The model is constructed with full consideration of the realistic situation and has good interpretability
units.function: claim realism and interpretability together
units.reusable_pattern: Pair full consideration of the realistic situation with good interpretability.
information_order: full consideration and interpretability
reusable_elements: full consideration of the realistic situation
prohibited_generalizations: Do not split the two claims.

units.source_excerpt: The results prove that this improvement enables the model to simulate the trend very well
units.function: cite the results as proof of an improvement
units.reusable_pattern: Use the results prove that for a strength.
information_order: the results prove that
reusable_elements: The results prove that this improvement
prohibited_generalizations: Do not weaken prove.

units.source_excerpt: The consideration is very comprehensive: we analyzed the overall trends and the fluctuations around them
units.function: claim comprehensiveness by naming both levels
units.reusable_pattern: Support very comprehensive by listing the two levels examined.
information_order: very comprehensive then both levels
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim comprehensiveness without the two levels.

units.source_excerpt: The models are interlinked and corroborate each other
units.function: claim cross-model agreement
units.reusable_pattern: Use interlinked and corroborate each other for agreement across parts.
information_order: interlinked and corroborate
prohibited_generalizations: Do not assert agreement the paper does not claim.

units.source_excerpt: The distribution of EERIE predicted by the P&S model was clustered and agreed with the classifier
units.function: give the concrete instance of agreement
units.reusable_pattern: Name both models and the one word they agree on.
information_order: predicted by A clustered and consistent with B
reusable_elements: consistent with that of the classifier
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim agreement beyond EERIE.

units.source_excerpt: Considering that the amount of data is not very large, we did not use a model with many parameters, so overfitting is avoided
units.function: claim a negative virtue by what was refused
units.reusable_pattern: State the constraint, the refusal, then the problem avoided.
information_order: considering not large we did not so avoided
prohibited_generalizations: Do not claim a regularisation method the paper does not use.

units.source_excerpt: There is still a gap between the model and the reality
units.function: open a weakness with a blunt gap statement
units.reusable_pattern: Start a weakness with there is still a gap between.
information_order: there is still a gap between
reusable_elements: There is still a gap between the model and the reality
prohibited_generalizations: Do not soften the gap.

units.source_excerpt: Different people use different strategies and different vocabularies, but the P&S model does not consider this enough
units.function: name the omitted variation
units.reusable_pattern: State the variation, then but we did not sufficiently consider.
information_order: variation but not sufficiently considered
prohibited_generalizations: Do not invent a fix inside the weakness.

units.source_excerpt: The accuracy of the classifier is only 68%, which is not particularly good, probably because some word characteristics were omitted
units.function: give the number, the verdict and the suspected cause
units.reusable_pattern: Report only 68%, which is not particularly good, probably because.
information_order: number then verdict then probable cause
prohibited_generalizations: Do not defend the accuracy the paper criticises.

units.source_excerpt: We can use different algorithms for different strategies, different lexicons for different vocabularies, and an optimization to find the proportion of each type
units.function: propose an extension as a three-part can
units.reusable_pattern: List the three additions with we can.
information_order: we can use then use then calculate
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the extension as done.

units.source_excerpt: By modifying some parameters, this model can be applied to other games
units.function: claim transfer with a small change
units.reusable_pattern: Use by modifying some parameters, this model can be applied to.
information_order: by modifying can be applied to
prohibited_generalizations: Do not name the other games the paper leaves unnamed.

units.source_excerpt: Dear Sir/Madam: Hello, we are a group of Wordle fanatics
units.function: open the letter with a salutation and a self-description
units.reusable_pattern: Open with Dear Sir/Madam, then who the writers are.
information_order: salutation then we are
prohibited_generalizations: Do not open the letter with results.

units.source_excerpt: We wake up every day to new Wordle puzzles on your app
units.function: establish the writers as users
units.reusable_pattern: Place the writers inside the product before any advice.
information_order: we wake up every day to
prohibited_generalizations: Do not skip the user stance.

units.source_excerpt: The game has certainly brought a lot of joy to our daily lives, and we want to do something in return
units.function: give the motive for the work
units.reusable_pattern: Pair the benefit received with the wish to return it.
information_order: certainly brought joy and we want to
reusable_elements: has certainly brought a lot of joy
prohibited_generalizations: Do not open with the model.

units.source_excerpt: So we are building a mathematical model of all Twitter Wordle reports in 2022
units.function: connect the motive to the work with so
units.reusable_pattern: Use so we are building to move from motive to method.
information_order: so we are building
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the so.

units.source_excerpt: We hope our analysis can help your team improve Wordle
units.function: state the offer
units.reusable_pattern: Close the opening with we hope our analysis can help your team.
information_order: we hope can help your team
reusable_elements: We hope our analysis can help
prohibited_generalizations: Do not promise an improvement.

units.source_excerpt: Because the rules are fixed, perhaps the most (and only) challenging part is choosing an appropriate word
units.function: narrow the whole problem to one decision
units.reusable_pattern: Use perhaps the most (and only) challenging part to focus the letter.
information_order: because fixed perhaps the only challenge
reusable_elements: perhaps the most (and only) challenging part
prohibited_generalizations: Do not widen the letter beyond word choice.

units.source_excerpt: But how do we know if a word is appropriate enough? Is it better to be common or rare?
units.function: pose the client's questions as questions
units.reusable_pattern: Keep the client's problem as a run of direct questions.
information_order: but how do we know then is it better
reusable_elements: Is it better to be common or rare
prohibited_generalizations: Do not convert the questions into statements.

units.source_excerpt: First, we extract 12 indicators. Next, we modelled the trend. Then we try to predict the distribution.
units.function: retell the paper with first next then
units.reusable_pattern: Retell the paper in the letter with First, Next, Then, not with section numbers.
information_order: first next then
prohibited_generalizations: Do not copy the summary sheet into the letter.

units.source_excerpt: This model can predict future report numbers, for example reports on 1 March fall between [17760, 20976]
units.function: give one example number inside the prose
units.reusable_pattern: Attach the interval with for example.
information_order: can predict for example interval
prohibited_generalizations: Do not give the corrected interval here; the letter prints the first one.

units.source_excerpt: It can also explain player structures, and shows that most Wordle players now are loyal players
units.function: add a second use of the same model
units.reusable_pattern: Add the structural finding with it can also.
information_order: it can also explain
prohibited_generalizations: Do not correct structues.

units.source_excerpt: For any word, for example eerie, the distribution is expected to be (0, 0, 9%, 29%, 45%, 14%, 3%)
units.function: reuse the same example word across the letter
units.reusable_pattern: Keep eerie as the running example and the distribution in parentheses.
information_order: for any word e.g. then tuple
prohibited_generalizations: Do not change the distribution.

units.source_excerpt: The example eerie used above is of course labelled hard
units.function: confirm the example with of course
units.reusable_pattern: Use of course for a result the letter treats as expected.
information_order: of course labelled
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop of course.

units.source_excerpt: The last piece of the puzzle is the relationship between difficulty and the number of reports
units.function: name the final link with a puzzle metaphor
units.reusable_pattern: Call the last part the last piece of the puzzle.
information_order: the last piece of the puzzle is
reusable_elements: The last piece of the puzzle
prohibited_generalizations: Do not use the metaphor before the last item.

units.source_excerpt: Although this is a little counterintuitive, we ultimately explain it by saying that Normal Mode players share less when the word is hard
units.function: concede then explain
units.reusable_pattern: Open with although a little counterintuitive, then we ultimately explain by saying.
information_order: although counterintuitive we ultimately explain
reusable_elements: Although this is a little counterintuitive
we ultimately explain this by saying
prohibited_generalizations: Do not drop the concession.

units.source_excerpt: For your team, we wonder if our model can be used to predict player response before each puzzle is released
units.function: turn the model into an offer
units.reusable_pattern: Address the reader with for your team, we wonder if.
information_order: for your team we wonder if
reusable_elements: For your team, we wonder if
prohibited_generalizations: Do not write the offer as an instruction.

units.source_excerpt: A difficult word might not be appropriate, as it might discourage intermediate players from sharing
units.function: give the practical warning
units.reusable_pattern: State the warning with might, twice.
information_order: might not be appropriate as it might
reusable_elements: might not be an appropriate choice
prohibited_generalizations: Do not turn might into will.

units.source_excerpt: We recommend words with only one or two indicators that make them difficult, so the word does not fall into the hard category
units.function: give the concrete recommendation
units.reusable_pattern: Use we recommend, then the limit, then so.
information_order: we recommend then limit then so
reusable_elements: We recommend words with only one or two indicators
prohibited_generalizations: Do not recommend a specific word.

units.source_excerpt: If the indicators that make words difficult vary from day to day, it might give daily players a sense of freshness
units.function: add a second recommendation as a conditional benefit
units.reusable_pattern: Give the variation as if, then the benefit with might even.
information_order: if vary then might even
reusable_elements: might even give daily Wordle players a sense of freshness
prohibited_generalizations: Do not present the benefit as certain.

units.source_excerpt: We would be happy to discuss the game further with your team. We look forward to playing great Wordle puzzles in the future.
units.function: close with an offer and a wish
units.reusable_pattern: End with we would be happy to, then we look forward to.
information_order: happy to discuss then look forward to
reusable_elements: We would be happy to discuss
prohibited_generalizations: Do not add a sign-off the paper does not use.

units.source_excerpt: Yours sincerely, Team #2318036
units.function: sign the letter with the team number
units.reusable_pattern: Close with yours sincerely and the team number.
information_order: yours sincerely then team number
prohibited_generalizations: Do not omit the team number.

units.source_excerpt: The references run from Anderson and Meyer on Wordle strategy to the Wikipedia entry for Wordle
units.function: close on a numbered reference list mixing preprints and textbooks
units.reusable_pattern: Keep the list as numbered brackets from the reinforcement-learning preprint to the Wikipedia snapshot.
information_order: numbered list preprint to encyclopedia
prohibited_generalizations: Do not treat the reference list as models.

units.source_excerpt: Reference 5 prints Mathematic in Practice and Theory, and reference 4 names the venue in full
units.function: keep a printed defect in a reference
units.reusable_pattern: Record the printed venue spelling without repair.
information_order: printed venue as printed
prohibited_generalizations: Do not correct Mathematic.
